summary: This Wikipedia-style note traces the romantic and professional arc of Pam Beesly, a fictional character on the U.S. sitcom The Office, played by Jenna Fischer. It follows her from receptionist to saleswoman to office administrator, and her on-off relationship with Jim Halpert through their engagement, marriage, children and eventual departure from Dunder Mifflin. It also covers her growth in Season 3 and her plotlines involving art, Michael Scott and the Pratt Institute.
one_line: Wiki article on Pam Beesly, the receptionist-turned-saleswoman character in The Office and her relationship with Jim Halpert.
key_facts: Pam Beesly is a fictional character on the U.S. television sitcom The Office, played by Jenna Fischer.
Pam's counterpart in the original UK series of The Office is Dawn Tinsley.
Pam is initially the receptionist at the paper distribution company Dunder Mifflin, before becoming a saleswoman and eventually office administrator until her termination in the series finale.
Pam begins dating Jim Halpert in the fourth season, after the Season 4 opener reveals they are dating.
Jim and Pam marry at Niagara Falls in the highly anticipated, hour long episode 'Niagara'.
The ending of 'Niagara', in which co-workers dance down the aisle, imitates the viral YouTube video JK Wedding Entrance Dance.
Michael hooks up with Pam's mother the night of the wedding, and Pam and Jim break up during 'Double Date', where Pam slaps Michael.
In the Season 5 premiere 'Weight Loss', Pam begins a three-month course at the Pratt Institute, and Jim proposes in the pouring rain at a rest stop.
In 'Business Trip', Pam learns she is failing one class and decides to return home, saying she realized she hated graphic design and missed Scranton.
In 'Two Weeks', Pam agrees to become Michael's first saleswoman in The Michael Scott Paper Co.
In 'Company Picnic', Pam injures her ankle during the company volleyball tournament and is implied to be pregnant, confirmed in the Season 6 premiere 'Gossip'.
In Season 3's opener 'Gay Witch Hunt', it is revealed Pam did not marry Roy after all, and Jim transferred to the Stamford branch.
In Season 3, Pam moves into her own apartment, begins taking art classes, and buys a blue Toyota Yaris.
In the Season 3 episode 'The Job', Jim is interviewing for a job at Corporate in New York City when Pam's yogurt lid memento reminds him of her, and he withdraws and asks her out for dinner.
Karen quits soon after and becomes the regional manager at Dunder Mifflin's Utica branch.
In Season 9, Jim takes a second job in Philadelphia, straining the marriage, and the couple ultimately leave Dunder Mifflin together so Jim can pursue his dream job.
